summary:
No Assam-specific statute on gender recognition, criminal law or facilities appears in the sources reviewed, and the national framework therefore governs both visitors and residents in the state. The December 2021 parliamentary reply on Transgender Welfare Boards constituted under the 2019 Rules listed twelve states and union territories; Assam was not among them, so no state-level welfare board was identified for Assam at that date.

Complaint registration under the national Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act has been reachable in Assam. Two of the seven cases registered nationally under the Act in 2021 were registered in the state; the 2023 national tally recorded none in Assam. Both are raw counts, and the review that compiled them gives no population denominator for Assam, so the state's share cannot be converted into a rate or compared with other states on a per-capita basis.

The counts measure registration, not violence. The crime-data review of 30 January 2026 attributes the small national totals, 20 cases across 2019 to 2023, to police-registration bias rather than to an absence of incidents. For a visitor, the Assam rows establish only that a complaint can be filed and recorded in the state.
tangentialFactors:
The one Assam-specific channel the sources document is complaint registration under the national Act. No state court ruling, state health or facility rule, state custodial practice, or enforcement incident in Assam appears in the inventory, so the state's own administrative posture on trans residents is not visible in this material.

Assam's registered count moved from two cases in 2021 to none in 2023. The review's caution that registration practice rather than incident levels drives these tallies applies to any reading of that movement as a change in safety.
localsOnly:
Residents have no state-level transgender welfare board documented as of the December 2021 reply, so the state-coordinated route to housing support, surgery in public hospitals or pension benefits that a board provides was not identified in Assam; welfare access runs through the national framework instead.

Police registration of complaints under the national Act does occur in the state: two cases in 2021, none in 2023. Whether Assam has since constituted a board, or issued its own welfare, health or recognition rules, is not established by the sources reviewed.
outOfScopeNotes:
The 2025 survey figures cited by the review, 27.2% for physical violence and 22.3% for sexual violence, are not broken down by state and carry no general-population comparison, so they cannot be presented as an Assam rate.

The welfare-board position rests on a parliamentary reply of December 2021. No later source in the inventory confirms that Assam still has no board, or records one being constituted.

The registered-case data predate the March 2026 amendment to the national recognition law, so they are not evidence about how the amended scheme operates in Assam.

No source in the inventory records Assam's share of the trans population, prison or custody policy inside the state, or any Assam police or state government statement on trans residents.
